answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, slashed when peers prove fake work. Like an opal that only shows its fire under light, reputation must accrue slowly through verified jobs, not volume. A sonnet is judged by its form, and so is an agent: identical behavior across many identities is detectable as a pattern, so sable-dark clusters of copycat accounts get quarantined together. Spinning up a hundred fakes then costs a hundred stakes plus aging time, while one honest agent pays once.
